summary:
Mars → Earth Analog Finder is an interactive web application that pairs locations on Mars with their closest environmental matches on Earth (and vice versa) to help scientists and engineers identify real-world testing sites for space missions.

Core Functionality: Users can click anywhere on synchronized 2D maps and 3D globes—or input coordinates—to compare conditions across 25 Martian regions and 23 extreme Earth analog sites.

Data & Physics: It consolidates planetary physics models and orbital data from 11 archives across five major space agencies (NASA, ESA, CSA, Copernicus, and JAXA).

Key Features: Calculates local elevation, temperature, pressure, water-ice access, and habitability; ranks matches using customizable weights; allows reverse-searching from Earth to Mars; and links directly to NASA Worldview and Earthdata satellite imagery.

Impact: Streamlines mission planning, reduces hardware testing risks, and makes planetary science accessible for researchers and students.
details: Mars → Earth Analog Finder is a browser-based tool that matches any coordinate on Mars with its closest environment on Earth (and vice versa) to help researchers and mission planners find real-world test sites for space hardware. How It Works & Data: Using 25 Mars regions and 23 Earth sites calibrated against 11 space agency archives (NASA PDS, Earthdata, Worldview, LRO Diviner, ESA, CSA, Copernicus, JAXA) and 7 Mars rovers/landers, the app interpolates local elevation, temperature, pressure, and ice access to rank Earth matches ($0\text{–}100\%$) across 5 adjustable weights. Delivered Features: Interactive 2D maps and 3D globes for both Mars and Earth, two-way "Reverse Match" lookup, live satellite links (Worldview/Earthdata/Google Maps), and a real-time 8-axiom verification panel. Limitations & Future Plans: Uses regional interpolation and annual averages for first-pass screening; future updates will add high-res HiRISE hazard maps and seasonal weather sliders. Tech Stack: Single-file, zero-dependency HTML5, CSS3, SVG, and vanilla JavaScript (Canvas 2D) that runs in any browser.
